target_customer: Startups and teams wanting a lightweight realtime company wiki and shared notes
problem: Teams needed a fast way to write and organize notes and docs together in realtime without heavy wiki or office suite overhead.
business_model: Freemium SaaS for teams, paid plans for company wikis

founders.name: Igor Kofman
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the only founder and says he later co-led Act Now Coalition. No education or prior employers listed there.

competitors.name: Etherpad
competitors.what: Open source realtime collaborative text editor that Hackpad was built from
competitors.traction_then: Well known among developers and used in many deployments

competitors.name: Google Docs
competitors.what: Browser based document editing with collaboration

technical_complexity.rationale: Realtime collaborative editing is hard to get right, but Hackpad started from the open source Etherpad codebase, which cut the core research work for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: The code was a fork of open source Etherpad and Google Docs already offered shared editing, so defensibility rested on product feel and stored company wikis.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Dropbox acquired Hackpad in April 2014, folded the team into what became Dropbox Paper, announced the Hackpad shutdown for July 2017 and open sourced the code.

market_need_then: Teams used Etherpad and Google Docs for shared notes, and a 2013 post by investor Fred Wilson described Hackpad as filling a gap with follow and notify features. Customers listed on its site included Airbnb, Stripe and Upworthy.

branding.community_and_virality: Used as a company wiki by startups such as Airbnb, Stripe and Upworthy per press at the time of the Dropbox deal.

brand_strength.rationale: Known inside the startup community and listed with recognizable customers, but no source shows press about the brand itself, a mascot or merch.

outcome_analysis: Hackpad built a realtime wiki on top of Etherpad and won startup customers such as Airbnb and Stripe with a two person team. Dropbox bought it in April 2014 for an undisclosed price and used the team to build Paper, so the product outcome was a soft landing inside a larger company and the service was later shut down in 2017.
notes: hackpad.com returned HTTP 503 when fetched. CB Insights listed odd small rounds (about 20K total) and Crunchbase rows were obscured, so no round is recorded as verified. Some secondary sources name Alex Graveley as a co-founder, but the YC page lists only Igor Kofman, so he is not recorded. Dropbox price undisclosed.
